comparison: Both evaluate antibody validation experiments (C4, C15-C20) and reach the same SUPPORTED conclusion. OpenEval emphasizes the multiple experimental approaches demonstrating antibody non-specificity, while peer reviewers acknowledge the comprehensiveness and validity of these findings, with all reviewers praising the meticulous approach.

Both address claims about lack of phosphorylation (C5, C21-C26), but reach different conclusions. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED based on converging orthogonal techniques (pan-phosphotyrosine antibody, Phos-tag gels, LC-MS/MS). Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about lack of positive controls, potential detection limits of mass spectrometry without enrichment, and possible interference from GFP tags.

Both evaluate electrophysiology data (C27, C64), but disagree on interpretation. OpenEval finds the functional evidence SUPPORTED and consistent with biochemical findings. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, questioning whether GFP-tagged PANX1 is properly localized to plasma membrane, whether observed currents are from tagged or endogenous PANX1, and whether the construct requires cleavage for proper function.

Both evaluate critical assessment of prior work (C55-C56) and reach SUPPORTED conclusions. OpenEval notes these observations are consistent with current findings about antibody non-specificity. Peer reviewers acknowledge the concerns but note that previous studies presented additional supporting data beyond just the commercial antibodies, though they don't directly refute the specific observations.

Both evaluate deglycosylation experiments (C47-C51) and agree these are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the confirmation of N-linked glycosylation through PNGase F treatment. Peer reviewers do not challenge these technical observations, describing the work as meticulous and well-controlled.

Both evaluate acknowledgment of limitations and alternative hypotheses (C57-C61) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these demonstrate scientific rigor in interpretation. Peer reviewers appreciate these acknowledgments and see value in the work prompting reexamination of earlier studies and spawning new function-oriented research.

Both address structural analysis and conservation data (C10-C14), reaching SUPPORTED conclusions. OpenEval emphasizes the structural demonstration of buried residues and reasonable inference about conformational changes. Peer reviewers do not challenge the structural analysis, noting the breadth and comprehensive approach of the experiments.

OpenEval evaluates claims about Src variants (C28-C29, C46) as SUPPORTED based on prior literature and established properties. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological context claims.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C3, C6-C9, C30-C43, C52-C54) as SUPPORTED based on citations to prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background context claims, though peer reviewers implicitly accept the motivation and significance context.
